name: Order of the Secretary of the Interior, July 10, 1865, on reserves for the Washo (Royce area 473)
citation: Order of the Secretary of the Interior, July 10, 1865 (Royce schedule p. 836)
nations: Washoe Tribe of Nevada and California (Wá·šiw)
promises: Not a treaty. Royce records that the country claimed by the Washoes was taken possession of by settlers between 1855 and 1865 without purchase of their title by the United States.

On July 1, 1865 Agent Lockhart recommended two reserves of 360 acres each in Carson and Washoe valleys; on July 10 the Secretary of the Interior directed that two reserves totalling 8 sections be set apart; in October Agent Parker reported no suitable lands remained vacant, and no further action was taken (Royce p. 837).

breaches.what: The government's own land cession survey records that the Washo country was taken by settlers between 1855 and 1865 without the United States buying the Indians' title, and that the reserves ordered in 1865 were never set apart.

today: No reserve was set apart under the 1865 order (Royce). Washoe lands today are later allotments, colonies and purchases; not traced here.

nationVoice.summary: The Tribe's history page says that in the California gold rush and the Nevada silver rush that followed, thousands of miners and immigrants flooded Washoe lands within a few years and stayed, depleting the resources the people lived on: logging stripped the forests and the Pine Nut Mountains, Lake Tahoe's native cutthroat trout fishery was reduced to nothing, and livestock replaced native game.

openQuestions: The Washoe Tribe's own account was not located (its website did not appear in searches).

The 1959 opinion left the Nevada taking date open; the Commission's 1969 valuation opinion (21 Ind. Cl. Comm. 447, October 31, 1969) used December 31, 1862 as the Nevada valuation date and found the United States liable for $5,053,350 less allowable offsets.
The day of the 1970 final award is smudged in the scan; the date given is the collection's date.

Audit 2026-11-08 (round 12): Docket 288 checked: the 1959 interlocutory order holds that the Washoe proved Indian title, that California title was acquired March 3, 1853, and that the United States paid nothing; the final award nets $4,959,350 after a $94,000 offset; Royce's quote is exact. The open line on the 1969 valuation decision was filled in from that opinion (OSU id 2531).

plain.promised: Not a treaty. In 1865 the Interior Secretary ordered two small reserves set apart for the Washoe, after settlers had taken over their country.
plain.happened: The government's own 1899 survey says settlers took the Washoe country without the United States buying it, and no reserve was found. The Indian Claims Commission held in 1959 the United States took Washoe title without paying.
plain.today: In 1970 the Commission awarded the Washoe $4,959,350 after deductions.
